`final class JsonFiles`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.utils.json` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [JsonFiles.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/utils/json/JsonFiles.java)

Reads and writes the JSON files of JOID safely: atomic writes, and a damaged file set aside instead of lost.

## Description

The stores and the remembered properties of the UIs keep their files with it.
Every failure prints a `[JOID]` warning instead of throwing.

## Learn more

- [Stores and remembered properties](/use/learn/state/stores-and-properties/)
- [Where JOID stores files](/use/learn/running/files/)

## Method details

<a id="JsonFiles-method-read"></a>

### read

`JsonObject read(File file, String consequence)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

Returns the JSON object of `file`, or `null` when the file does not exist or cannot be used.
A file that holds no JSON object is renamed to `<name>.corrupt`; the warning ends with `consequence`, which says what happens instead.

<a id="JsonFiles-method-write"></a>

### write

`void write(File file, String json)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

Writes `json` to `file` through a temporary file in the same folder, created when missing, then moves it in place in one step, so a crash never leaves half a file.

<a id="JsonFiles-method-keep"></a>

### keep

`void keep(File file, String failure, String consequence)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

Renames `file` to `<name>.corrupt`, replacing an older one, and prints a warning with `failure` and `consequence`.
